Let me analyze this conflict.

Axis: applicant
- Register: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi"
- Document: "ESIT Elektronik Ltd. Şti."

The register's version is the full legal name: "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi" (which in Turkish would be "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi"). The document's version is the abbreviated form: "ESIT Elektronik Ltd. Şti." which is the standard Turkish abbreviation for "ESIT Elektronik Limited Şirketi" — but wait, the abbreviation "Ltd. Şti." only covers "Limited Şirketi" part, while the full name includes "Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret". So "ESIT Elektronik Ltd. Şti." is a common short form of "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler İmalat ve Ticaret Limited Şirketi". The core identifying token "ESIT Elektronik" matches. This is legal-suffix drift / abbreviation — same entity.

Which best_value? The rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. For same-entity, what's the best value? The rules don't explicitly say for same-entity name cases, but for "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form." For legal names, presumably the fuller legal name is more canonical. The register gives the full legal name; the document gives an abbreviated form. The fused record should carry the full legal name — best_value = register's value.

Actually, one might argue the document is the legal instrument, so the document's value should be used. But for same-entity verdicts, the rules only specify best_value for number/year format (register's canonical form). For name drift, the fuller form seems better. Also the register is the canonical database. I'd say best_value = "ESIT Elektronik Sistemler Imalat ve Ticaret Limited Sirketi".

Verdict: same-entity.
